answer: Every agent keeps a kernel ledger signed only by its own key, plus a lantern that stamps each outbound action with a short light-hash. Before any peer pays that agent, it re-verifies the stamp; so when a sybil zephyr of a thousand fresh keys floods the network, every key must still burn the same verification work and time-lock, and attacker cost scales linearly with headcount while one honest identity's long history amortizes the cost for it.
